title: Hector's Farewell to Andromache
text:
During the Trojan War, Hector, Troy's greatest warrior, came back from the battlefield into the city. He looked for his wife Andromache at home, but she had gone to the walls with their baby son Astyanax to watch the fighting. He found her near the Scaean Gate.

She took his hand and pleaded with him. Achilles had killed her father and her seven brothers, she said; her mother was dead too. Hector was now father, mother, brother and husband to her. She begged him to stay on the walls and not make her a widow and their son an orphan.

Hector answered that he would be ashamed before the Trojans if he hung back like a coward. He knew in his heart that Troy would fall, and what grieved him most was not his own death but the thought of her being led away as a slave.

He reached out for his son. But the baby shrank back, crying, frightened by the bronze helmet and its nodding horsehair crest. Hector and Andromache both laughed. Hector took off the helmet and set it on the ground, kissed his son and rocked him in his arms, and prayed that the boy would one day be greater than his father. Then he handed him back to his wife, who smiled through her tears, and went out to the war.
lesson: Duty can pull us away from the people we love, but in the moments we have, take off the helmet. Children need to see the person, not the armor.
